target_customer: Small home service and trade businesses (plumbing, painting, landscaping, roofing, HVAC) in the US
problem: Home service pros rely on word of mouth and struggle to be found online, look trustworthy, get booked and get paid without hiring marketing help.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription for local service businesses
product_category: Marketing, website and booking platform for home service businesses (originally a video-call app for plumbers)

founders.name: Nick Ornitz
education: Harvard Business School, one year before taking leave
founders.background_notes: YC page says he worked and consulted in construction technology, go-to-market and sales; employers not named. TechCrunch says his siblings run service businesses and he previously worked with home improvement retailers.

founders.name: Shannon Kay
education: Harvard dual degree program (MS Engineering Sciences and MBA), first year completed
founders.background_notes: YC page describes a data, analytics and systems engineering background; employers not named.

technical_complexity.rationale: At founding it was a video-call and scheduling app, standard web and mobile engineering. The later generative AI website and assistant products add moderate complexity but were not the founding product.

defensibility.rationale: Website builders and field service tools were copyable; the main stickiness comes from customers' sites, listings and payments living on the platform, plus a done-for-you service approach.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No source shows an incumbent copying or buying it. By 2025 the company names Rebolt, Jobber and Housecall Pro as rivals on its own comparison pages.

market_need_then: The founders report that plumbers liked video calls but needed more jobs and had no way to grow beyond word of mouth (TechCrunch 2022). Home service is a large, digitally underserved segment of small businesses.

branding.name_origin: ProPhone was the original name for a video-call product for pros. Topline Pro was chosen in 2022 as the company shifted to helping pros grow; the company post gives no specific trigger beyond that.
branding.domain_note: Uses toplinepro.com, a .com with a Pro suffix; no purchase price found.

identity.mascot_or_character: Sidekick, the AI assistant, is a product persona rather than a mascot
identity.voice_and_tone: Teammate framing: 'don't have to do it all alone', 'done for you', tagline 'The AI for local service pros'

branding.brand_signature: Done for you positioning and the Sidekick AI assistant

rebrands.why: Company said it had evolved from video calls to helping home service pros get discovered, trusted and booked; ProPhone no longer described the product.

brand_strength.rationale: Solid trade-focused positioning and a clear tagline, but no evidence of press about the brand, merch or community. Name is descriptive and somewhat generic.

pivots.from: ProPhone, video calls connecting plumbers with homeowners
pivots.to: Topline Pro, subscription website and marketing product for home service businesses
pivots.why: Plumbers liked video calls but needed more jobs and growth beyond word of mouth.

outcome_analysis: The founding video-call idea did not become the business; the team pivoted in early 2022 to a website and marketing subscription for home service pros, raised a 5 million seed in October 2022 and a 27 million Series B in August 2025 with the company claiming over 6,000 customers. The generative AI wave gave the pivot a timing tailwind. The company is still active.
notes: YC page links a TechCrunch article for a 12M raise in July 2023; I could not open a source confirming amount or investors, so it is not recorded as a round (unverified). One database dates the seed to 2022-08; press says October 2022. Series B lead is disputed between aggregators (ZoomInfo names Flybridge); Pulse2 says Northzone. Competition at founding: no source dated near January 2021 found, list left empty; the 2022 TechCrunch article names Finli, Zuper, Fuzey and Puls but those are 2022 context. Rounds list may be incomplete.
